priorStories.headline: Microsoft outage disrupts Outlook and other services
priorStories.body:
An outage disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services Thursday. Microsoft said some servers unexpectedly became unavailable, straining the remaining infrastructure.

By 6:57 p.m. Eastern, the company reported limited recovery after returning some servers to service and rerouting traffic. Full restoration had not been established in that update.

Nearly 130,000 Outlook reports appeared on Downdetector near the earlier peak. Those were user reports, not a verified count of affected accounts.

priorStories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
priorStories.body:
Nvidia said Thursday that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive and that chief financial officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. His departure followed disclosures of extramarital relationships.

The board named Harvey C. Jones chairman and said it would consider both internal and external candidates for a permanent chief executive.

candidates.summary: Microsoft reported early stabilization and capacity improvements on November 13 as recovery work continued on the Microsoft 365 outage that began November 12. Full restoration had not been established. Earlier recovery attempts had not worked as expected, and the disruption continued to affect Outlook, Teams and other services. Microsoft said it had no indication that malicious activity caused the outage.
candidates.title: Microsoft reports early stabilization as global service outage continues

candidates.summary: Microsoft reported broader recovery in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe and improving conditions in Asia Pacific on November 13. The company also said email queues had significantly decreased and were approaching normal levels. Some users could still experience intermittent access problems or delayed email delivery; full restoration had not been established. The Microsoft 365 disruption began November 12.
candidates.title: Microsoft reports wider recovery and reduced email queues as outage continues

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released October producer-price data at 8:30 a.m. Eastern on November 13. The final-demand Producer Price Index increased 0.3% from September, seasonally adjusted, and 6.5% over the preceding 12 months, unadjusted—the largest annual increase since November 2022. September's monthly increase was revised to 1.4%.
candidates.title: US producer prices rise 0.3% in October and 6.5% over a year

candidates.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on November 13 afternoon after communications problems affected regional air traffic control centers. Departing aircraft were ordered to remain on the ground, while inbound international flights were to be handled individually. Officials said airborne flights were accounted for and continued landing. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the cause remained under investigation and there was no indication at that point of an attack. No connection to the Microsoft outage had been established.
candidates.title: FAA halts departures nationwide after air traffic control communications outage

candidates.summary: The FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on November 13, allowing departures to resume after more than four hours of disruption. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said radar data and communications had become unstable across air traffic facilities; the agency had not lost all telecommunications. Officials attributed the disruption to overloaded older equipment, with the underlying cause still under investigation. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators had found no evidence of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft outage. Flight schedules remained disrupted after the restriction ended.
candidates.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after communications disruption

candidates.summary: Microsoft marked its Exchange Online and related Microsoft 365 incidents as service restored late on November 13; the suite incident's final update was recorded at 11:17 p.m. Eastern. Earlier evening updates reported continued recovery while engineers monitored accumulated email and remaining dependent-service problems. Microsoft identified the preliminary cause as an issue introduced during an earlier network-capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change, and said it was unrelated to cyberattacks or AI agents. Its final notice retained language about restoring remaining customers and regions, so the status designation does not independently establish that every residual problem had ended.
candidates.title: Microsoft marks outage incidents restored late Friday and identifies preliminary cause
